title: Support + Engineering SLAs by Customer Tier (Escalation Playbook v2)
author: Dev Patel
content:
## Purpose
This page defines **Support** and **Engineering/SRE engagement** SLAs by customer tier for Redwood Inference. It is intended to:
- Set consistent expectations for **first response**, **update cadence**, and **time-to-mitigation**.
- Clarify **after-hours** coverage by tier.
- Define **escalation triggers** (what constitutes an escalation) and when a support escalation becomes an **incident**.

> Note: This page describes **internal operating targets**. Contractual commitments are defined in the customer’s MSA/SOW and any published SLA addendum. If there is a mismatch, escalate to CS leadership + PM (see PM-612).

---

## Definitions & clock rules
### Severity mapping (reference)
We use a combined scheme:
- **P0 / Sev0**: Critical outage or severe widespread impact
- **P1 / Sev1**: Major degradation / high customer impact
- **P2 / Sev2**: Limited degradation / workaround available
- **P3 / Sev3**: Minor issue / how-to / cosmetic / low urgency
- **P4**: Requests, feedback, non-urgent items (handled via product/process)

See: **Severity Matrix & Triage Criteria** for concrete examples (5xx, timeouts, streaming disconnects, throttling/429s, Dedicated capacity shortfalls, Private SSO/audit-log issues).

### What starts the SLA clock
- **Support SLAs** start when a ticket is created **with minimum triage info** OR when Support has enough info to act.
- **Engineering/SRE engagement SLAs** start when Support files an escalation with **required fields completed** (see Support ticket template).

If required fields are missing, Support must:
1) respond to the customer with a targeted request for missing items (request IDs, region, model, timestamps, SDK version, error sample), and
2) mark the ticket as **“Blocked: awaiting customer info”** (clock pauses until info is received).

### Business hours (BH)
Unless otherwise noted:
- **BH** = Mon–Fri, **08:00–18:00 PT**, excluding Redwood company holidays.
- “24x7” means coverage via **on-call rotation**.

---

## Tier taxonomy
- **Self-serve**: Hosted API users without a Dedicated/Private contract; standard support.
- **Dedicated**: Reserved capacity customers (dedicated GPU pools); typically contract-backed expectations.
- **Private**: VPC / on-prem deployments; may involve customer-managed networking/IdP and stricter change control.
- **Enterprise**: Top-tier contractual customers (may be Hosted, Dedicated, or Private) with enhanced comms and after-hours handling.

---

## SLA summary tables
### Table A — Support SLAs (customer-facing operations)
All times are targets unless the contract specifies otherwise.

| Tier | First response (P0/P1) | First response (P2/P3) | Update frequency (P0) | Update frequency (P1) | Update frequency (P2/P3) | Time-to-mitigation target (P0) | After-hours expectations |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Self-serve | P0: 1 BH hour (best effort), P1: 4 BH hours | P2: 1 BH day, P3: 2 BH days | Every 2 hours (BH) | Twice daily (BH) | P2: daily (BH), P3: every 2–3 BH days | P0: same BH day (best effort) | No guaranteed after-hours. If clear platform-wide issue, Support may post status-page link + next BH update.
| Dedicated | P0: 30 min (24x7), P1: 2 hours (BH) | P2: 1 BH day, P3: 2 BH days | Every 60 min (until stable), 24x7 | Every 4 hours (BH) | P2: daily (BH), P3: every 2–3 BH days | P0: 4 hours | P0 is 24x7. P1 after-hours is best effort unless contract states otherwise.
| Private | P0: 30 min (24x7), P1: 2 hours (BH) | P2: 1 BH day, P3: 2 BH days | Every 60 min (until stable), 24x7 | Every 4 hours (BH) | P2: daily (BH), P3: every 2–3 BH days | P0: 4 hours (may require customer action if root cause is in customer-managed infra) | P0 is 24x7 coordination. For Private, comms must explicitly call out dependencies on customer networking/IdP changes.
| Enterprise | P0: 15 min (24x7), P1: 1 hour (BH) | P2: 8 BH hours, P3: 1 BH day | Every 30 min (until stable), 24x7 | Every 2 hours (BH) | P2: daily (BH), P3: every 2 BH days | P0: 2 hours | 24x7 for P0 (and P1 if contract specifies). CS/TAM may join comms; avoid speculative ETAs.

Notes:
- “Time-to-mitigation” means a meaningful risk reduction (rollback, failover, config change, rate-limit adjustment, disabling a bad route/model version, enabling a workaround), not necessarily a full fix.
- For Self-serve: if issue is widespread (multi-customer, multi-region) Support should guide customers to the **status page** and consolidate updates.

---

### Table B — Engineering & SRE engagement SLAs (internal)
These SLAs specify how quickly Engineering/SRE should engage once Support escalates with required fields.

| Severity | Triggering tier(s) | Who engages | Ack SLA | Initial investigation SLA | Mitigation / action-plan SLA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 / Sev0 | Dedicated, Private, Enterprise (and any widespread platform issue) | SRE on-call (incident lead) + owning eng team | 10 minutes (24x7) | 30 minutes: confirm scope + suspected component + immediate mitigations | 60 minutes: mitigation in progress or clear plan with next update time
| P1 / Sev1 | Dedicated, Private, Enterprise | SRE on-call or owning on-call (per ownership map); Support Eng as triage partner | 30 minutes (BH), best effort after-hours unless contract requires | 2 hours (BH): reproduce/confirm + identify likely cause | 1 BH day: mitigation deployed or workaround validated and shared
| P2 / Sev2 | All tiers | Owning eng team via normal queue; SRE only if reliability risk | 1 BH day | 2 BH days: diagnose + propose fix/workaround | 5 BH days (target): fix scheduled or KB workaround published
| P3 / Sev3 / P4 | All tiers | Support + Product/Eng backlog | 2 BH days | As scheduled | As scheduled

Operational notes:
- If a P1 is trending toward P0 (rapidly increasing error rate, multiple enterprise accounts, safety/security concerns), **upgrade severity** and engage SRE immediately.
- SRE engagement is appropriate when there is a strong chance the issue is systemic (routing, gateway, scheduler, runtime, region capacity) or when we need coordinated mitigation.

---

## Escalation triggers by tier (what constitutes an escalation)
Use this section to decide when a ticket must move from “Support handling” to “Engineering/SRE escalation.” These triggers are additive; Support may escalate earlier with strong evidence.

### Universal triggers (all tiers)
Escalate to Engineering/SRE when any of the following are true:
- **Potential platform incident**: elevated 5xx, widespread timeouts, region degradation, or model fleet issues affecting multiple customers.
- **Data integrity / security**: suspected auth bypass, cross-tenant data exposure, unexpected access to audit logs, or any security incident indicators.
- **No safe workaround** and customer impact is ongoing.
- **Reproducible bug** with clear request IDs and timestamps.

### Self-serve triggers
Escalate when:
- The issue appears **systemic** (multiple independent reports, dashboards indicate regional regression).
- There is a credible report of **billing/usage metering error** impacting multiple accounts.
- Customer is blocked on a critical launch and the issue maps to a known platform defect (Support Eng to validate).

Self-serve typically does **not** trigger paging for single-account issues unless there is evidence of a broader outage.

### Dedicated triggers
Escalate when:
- **Capacity shortfall**: customer cannot reach committed throughput, persistent queueing, or sustained latency above SLO despite expected traffic pattern.
- **Latency spikes/noisy neighbor suspicion**: correlated with host/pool saturation signals or cluster scheduling anomalies.
- **Routing/fallback misbehavior**: requests routed to wrong region/tier/model variant vs policy.

Paging guidance: P0 and high-confidence P1 can page SRE (see Table B) if impact is material.

### Private triggers
Escalate when:
- **SSO/SAML/OIDC login failures** affecting admin access or broad user access.
- **Networking/regression**: private endpoint connectivity issues, DNS/cert problems, egress restrictions causing model pulls/telemetry failures.
- **Audit-log pipeline issues** (missing events, delayed delivery) with compliance implications.

Important: Private often involves customer-managed components; escalation must include a clear list of “Redwood-owned” vs “customer-owned” checks.

### Enterprise triggers
Escalate when:
- Customer declares a **production incident** and expects rapid comms cadence.
- Multiple internal stakeholders are involved (CS/TAM + exec visibility).
- There is a risk of contractual SLA breach or customer is requesting formal incident handling / RCA.

Enterprise comms: coordinate with CS/TAM on tone, avoid assigning blame, and avoid promising fix times.

---

## After-hours rules & paging hygiene
To prevent alert fatigue while meeting commitments:
- **Page SRE on-call** for:
  - P0 / Sev0 (always, 24x7)
  - P1 only when contractually required, or when issue is likely systemic and urgent
- **Do not page** for P2/P3 unless explicitly directed by SRE lead during an active incident.
- When in doubt for P1 after-hours: post in **#eng-oncall** with required fields and ask for a go/no-go on paging.

See also: “Support escalation handoff to SRE and incident process” for incident declaration criteria.

---

## Update cadence guidance (what each update should include)
For any P0/P1 update to the customer, include:
- What we’re seeing (symptoms + scope)
- What we’re doing right now (actions taken)
- What the customer can do (safe mitigation/workaround, if any)
- When they should expect the next update

Avoid:
- speculative root causes (“likely AWS”, “probably GPU issue”) unless confirmed
- hard ETAs unless there is a validated mitigation path

---

## Examples (quick classification)
- **Enterprise + elevated 5xx in eu-west for pinned model** → P0/Sev0, page SRE, update every 30 min, mitigation via region failover/rollback.
- **Dedicated latency spikes during peak hours** → usually P1/Sev1; escalate to Dedicated/SRE if sustained and above contractual thresholds; validate noisy-neighbor diagnostics and autoscaling knobs.
- **Self-serve 429s after launch** → often P2 unless widespread; Support can resolve with quota verification + backoff guidance; escalate only if rate-limits appear misconfigured platform-wide.
- **Private SSO failures after IdP change** → P1 or P0 depending on scope (admin lockout = P0); engage Security/Private Deployments; document customer-owned checks.

---

## Ownership & exceptions
- If a customer requests commitments outside these tables, escalate to **CS leadership (Jasmine Liu / Rachel Kim)** and reference PM-612 for approved language.
- If the issue involves sensitive account details (Private/regulated workloads), apply **restricted handling** for artifacts (logs, request payloads) and avoid posting customer identifiers in broad Slack channels.

---

## Change log
- 2026-03-03: Adjusted Enterprise P0 first response target to 15 min; clarified P1 after-hours paging as contract-dependent.
- 2026-02-22: Added explicit clock pause rule when required escalation fields are missing.
- 2026-02-14: Initial v2 publication aligned with Support+SRE escalation policy sync.
